label: Fused prefill rmsnorm
mechanism: the four norm sites of every prefill layer move from the six-op torch reference chain (~36 bytes of HBM per element to do a 4-byte job) to B2.3's one-pass Triton rmsnorm, which has been in the tree and gated since bring-up but was wired into nothing
hypothesis: model.rmsnorm is the NUMERIC REFERENCE — six torch ops, bit-exact vs transformers (B2.2) — and after exp-0025 deleted the eager sconv chain it is the last bring-up-era eager chain on the prefill layer. It runs FOUR times per layer: the two hidden-width norms in layer_prefill (input_layernorm, post_attention_layernorm; model.py:587,603) and the two per-head norms in attn_prefill (q 64x128, k 16x128 on SWA layers / 8x128 on global ones; :494-495) — 264 calls per 66-layer traversal. Each call moves ~36 bytes per element to compute a row mean of squares: bf16->fp32 upcast (r2 w4), pow (r4 w4), the mean reduction (r4), the fp32 normalize (r4 w4), the downcast (r4 w2) and the weight multiply (r2 w2). The kernel does it in one pass — read bf16, reduce in fp32 in registers, write bf16 — for 4 bytes. Per token per layer the four sites carry 6144 + 6144 + 8192 + 2048 = 22,528 elements, so a canonical 6-row cohort (~4,200 tokens) moves ~200 GB per traversal it does not need to, on devices exp-0023's DEADENDS finding 1 shows are SATURATED during prefill. ONE VARIABLE: model.rmsnorm_prefill (new, +40 lines) plus the four call sites that read it, behind PYENGINE_FUSED_RMSNORM=0, which the function reads at CALL time; the torch reference is retained verbatim as model.rmsnorm and still serves every DECODE site, embed() and final_logits(), so nothing inside the CUDA-graph-captured step moves. The kernel itself (kernels/rmsnorm.py) is NOT rewritten — its only edit is the `with torch.cuda.device(x.device)` guard every other kernel wrapper in this engine already carries (attn_*, sconv_prefill, moe_gemm*, fp4_quant), because it was written for single-GPU bring-up tests and Triton validates pointers against the CURRENT context, so a layer-split traversal hits 'cannot be accessed from Triton' on the first layer that lives off device 0. That is launch configuration, not numerics: B2.3's gate is untouched. ARITHMETIC: same order, same fp32 accumulate, same downcast-before-weight-multiply; the ONLY divergence is the fp32 variance reduction (a register tree instead of torch's), i.e. the B3.1/B3.3 reduction-order class every fused kernel here has produced, bounded below at 2 bf16 ULP. EVIDENCE, ISOLATED (engine/pyengine/tests/t_fused_rmsnorm, GPU 4, B=6 T=1408, log /workspace/logs/t_fused_rmsnorm_exp0026_out.log): (arm a) EQUIVALENCE vs the torch chain at all four real site shapes x both dtypes — bf16 max ULP distance 2 at every shape with 51,904,398/51,904,512 (hidden), 69,205,841/69,206,016 (q) and 17,301,464/17,301,504 (k) elements BITWISE identical, max|delta| 3.125e-02 = one bf16 ULP at that magnitude, max rel 1.4e-02 on the isolated non-exact element; fp32 max 4 ULP, max|delta| 1.9e-06, max rel 3.5e-07. (arm b) two identical calls bitwise equal (the t_b3-adapted determinism arm; fixed grid, no atomics, no autotune). (arm c) SPEED, CUDA-event timed, interleaved arms after discarded warm-ups: hidden 6144 (x2 sites/layer) 0.548 -> 0.039 ms (13.9x), q norm 0.780 -> 0.284 ms (2.8x), k norm SWA 0.201 -> 0.075 ms (2.7x); an SWA layer's four sites go 2.076 -> 0.437 ms = 4.75x, -1.639 ms/layer, i.e. -0.108 s per 66-layer traversal at that shape, repeats agreeing to 0.001 ms. The two per-head sites are the WEAK ones (2.7-2.8x, ~0.5 TB/s): one program per 128-wide row is launch-bound, and a multi-row program is a separate, later variable — this experiment deliberately does not touch the kernel body. (arm d) LAYOUT: on a channel-major input (what the eager sconv chain hands the k-norm site when PYENGINE_FUSED_SCONV=0) still 2 ULP, and the output is contiguous. EVIDENCE, IN SITU on the real resident model through the real Scheduler, the arm exp-0011's rejection and exp-0018's null say must decide it (engine/pyengine/tests/t_fused_rmsnorm_insitu, GPUs 4-7, ONE resident load, layer split [16,17,16,17], 8 already-decoding residents plus a 6-row cohort at ISL 690-800, arms INTERLEAVED off/on/off/on after discarded warm-ups of BOTH arms; log /workspace/logs/t_fused_rmsnorm_insitu_exp0026_out.log): the PREFILL-only step (8 rows) goes 0.809 -> 0.717 s = 1.128x (-92 ms) and the MIXED step (6 prefill + 8 decode) 0.650 -> 0.582 s = 1.118x (-69 ms), the fused arm repeating to 0.001 s (0.717/0.717 and 0.582/0.581) and the eager arm to 0.017 s; DECODE-ONLY steps do not move (0.072/0.073/0.067 vs 0.073/0.075/0.068), as they must not. Schedule total 1.672 -> 1.514 s = 1.104x. BASE CHECK, from the same log: this run's EAGER arm (0.809 / 0.650 s) reproduces exp-0025's accepted FUSED arm (0.804 / 0.646 s) on the identical schedule, which is the evidence that this tree is the accepted lineage tip and not a stale base. NUMERICS, stated plainly: the in-situ tokens move (11 of 14 sequences over a 56-token schedule) because a 2-ULP shift 264 times per traversal compounds through the residual stream — the B3.1/B3.3 class, whose binding gate is D13, green below.
predicted_delta: +4.5 to +6.5% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s: 523-533 vs the accepted exp-0025 row 500.1 (merge bar 501.6). Cycle model from that row's own block (609 s, 2381 requests, 304,768 tokens): every request must be prefilled and exp-0017 admits cohorts of 6, so the box contains at least 2381/6 = ~397 grouped prefill traversals, each of which pays 264 rmsnorm calls. At the measured in-situ saving that is 397 x 0.069 = 27.4 s (mixed-step figure) to 397 x 0.092 = 36.5 s (prefill-step figure) of the 609 s box, i.e. 609/(609-S) = +4.7% to +6.4%. CALIBRATION on the row this replaces: exp-0025 measured -125/-163 ms on the same two arms and delivered +12.4% (445.0 -> 500.1), which back-solves to ~67 s removed from a 609 s box = ~0.17 s per traversal over ~390 traversals — so this box DOES convert the full per-traversal saving, and this experiment's saving is 0.55-0.56x of exp-0025's on both arms. WHY THIS IS NOT exp-0021 (predicted +3.7%, delivered +0.27%): that saving existed only on MIXED steps, and the box turned out to have roughly a tenth of the mixed steps the cohort model assumed. This saving is on EVERY prefill traversal — the prefill-only step moves -92 ms and the mixed step -69 ms, both measured, so the box's mix of step types cannot erase it. FLOOR CASE: a directly measured wall-clock difference on the real engine through the real Scheduler, not an extrapolation from a microbenchmark, and it does not depend on full cohorts — a 1-row traversal still makes all 264 calls, just on fewer rows, so admission fragmentation reduces the win proportionally rather than erasing it. It cannot read negative: the kernel moves strictly fewer bytes at every site shape measured and its output layout is contiguous, which is what its consumers want. The way it reads NULL is if the prefill term has fallen far enough after exp-0023 and exp-0025 that ~397 x 0.08 s is no longer a real share of the box — which would itself be worth knowing, and would move the next iteration's ranking off prefill and onto the decode step.

local_pregate.determinism: arm b of t_fused_rmsnorm (two identical kernel calls bitwise equal) and arm c of t_fused_rmsnorm_insitu (two identical fused SCHEDULES produce bitwise-identical token streams; the eager arm does too). The kernel has a fixed grid (one program per row), no atomics, no autotune and no shape-dependent branching beyond BLOCK_N = next_pow2(row width), so the kernel sequence is a pure function of the schedule. Nothing inside the CUDA-graph-captured decode step changes — the fused branch is on the prefill path only, and the decode-only step walls in the in-situ log are the control that shows it.
local_pregate.algebra: arm a is the algebra: same fp32 mean-of-squares, same rsqrt, same downcast to the input dtype BEFORE the weight multiply (InklingRMSNorm's order, modeling_inkling.py:99-113), same single bf16 round on store. The one difference is the fp32 reduction ORDER in the variance (a register tree vs torch's), which lands at <= 2 bf16 ULP with >= 99.9977% of elements bitwise identical at every real site shape, and <= 4 fp32 ULP. This is the same class of change B2.3 has gated since bring-up, when the kernel was written and validated against model.rmsnorm but never called.
local_pregate.syntax: py_compile clean. engine/pyengine/model.py +47/-4 (one kill switch, rmsnorm_prefill, four call sites), engine/pyengine/kernels/rmsnorm.py +11/-4 (device guard only, no numerics), engine/pyengine/tests/t_fused_rmsnorm.py and t_fused_rmsnorm_insitu.py new. harness/, configs/, goldens/, ledger, prompts, loop scripts untouched.
local_pregate.memory: strictly lower: the torch chain allocated three fp32 temporaries per call (the upcast, the squared tensor and the normalized tensor) plus the bf16 downcast; the kernel allocates one bf16 output. At the canonical cohort shape that is ~1.5 GB of transient allocation deleted per hidden-width site.
